title: Downloading reports and extracting text
text: gao.gov’s servers reject requests ordinary download tools, package uses curl-impersonate, variant curl gao.gov accepts. Install : platforms, prebuilt binaries available curl-impersonate releases page. binary different name location system, point package options(gao.curl_bin = "/path//curl_firefox147"). Everything else package works without , function needs remind instructions.
code: # Arch Linux sudo pacman -S curl-impersonate  # macOS brew install lexiforest/curl-impersonate/curl-impersonate

title: Downloading reports and extracting text
text: auto_download() one-stop function. Called arguments interactive session, walks choices — format, year range, confirmation total file count anything downloaded: specify everything front, scripts: Files land working directory: Downloads pause one second files (adjustable via sleep_time) polite gao.gov. full fiscal year typically hundred reports, plan several minutes per year hundred MB disk space.
code: library(gao)  auto_download() # All reports from fiscal years 2023-2024, as PDF auto_download(format = "pdf", year = 2023:2024, confirm = FALSE) gao_reports/ ├── pdf/ │   ├── gao-23-105043.pdf │   ├── gao-23-105177.pdf │   └── ... └── html/        (with format = "html" or "both")

title: Downloading reports and extracting text
text: format = "metadata" skips downloads entirely writes filtered metadata CSV — useful need report list spreadsheet another language:
code: auto_download(format = "metadata", year = 2020:2024, confirm = FALSE)

title: Downloading reports and extracting text
text: PDFs, extract_text() reads whole directory data.frame — one row per file, full text pages one string. requires pdftools package (install.packages("pdftools")). ready standard text-analysis tools — example, counting term mentions across reports: old reports scanned images rather digital text; yield NA text (warning listing affected files), filter .na(texts$text) analysis.
code: texts <- extract_text("gao_reports/pdf")  nrow(texts)          # one row per PDF texts$file[1]        # the filename texts$pages[1]       # its page count substr(texts$text[1], 1, 200)  # the first 200 characters of text mentions <- grepl("climate change", texts$text, ignore.case = TRUE) sum(mentions)

title: Downloading reports and extracting text
text: Filenames follow report URL slug, can connect extracted text back metadata gao_links(): Now every report’s text sits alongside topics, agencies, requesters, rest metadata — ready whatever question asking.
code: reports <- gao_links() reports$file <- paste0(basename(reports$url), ".pdf")  full <- merge(texts, reports, by = "file")

title: Download GAO Reports in One Step — auto_download
text: Convenience wrapper loads bundled report links, optionally filters fiscal year, downloads reports PDF, HTML, . Use format = "metadata" export CSV report metadata without downloading files.

title: Download GAO Reports in One Step — auto_download
code: auto_download(   format = NULL,   year = NULL,   download_dir = "gao_reports",   sleep_time = 1,   confirm = TRUE )

title: Download GAO Reports in One Step — auto_download
text: format Character. "pdf", "html", "", "metadata". "metadata" writes CSV report metadata without downloading files. NULL (default) prompts interactively; non-interactive sessions defaults "pdf". year Integer vector 4-digit fiscal years, e.g. 2024 2020:2024. NULL (default) prompts interactively; non-interactive sessions uses available years. download_dir Character. Base directory downloads. pdf/ /html/ subdirectories created beneath . sleep_time Numeric. Seconds pause downloads. confirm Logical. TRUE (default), prompts confirmation downloading. non-interactive sessions, confirm = TRUE raises error prevent accidental mass downloads – set confirm = FALSE explicitly.

title: Download GAO Reports in One Step — auto_download
text: "pdf", "html", "": invisible character vector downloaded file paths. "metadata": invisible path written CSV.

title: Download GAO Reports in One Step — auto_download
text: format = "pdf", "html", "" downloads files https://www.gao.gov requires curl-impersonate system binary. format = "metadata" reads bundled dataset works without .

title: Download GAO Reports in One Step — auto_download
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Interactive: walks through prompts auto_download()  # Non-interactive: download 2024 PDFs auto_download(format = "pdf", year = 2024, confirm = FALSE)  # Export metadata only (no file downloads) auto_download(format = "metadata", year = 2020:2024, confirm = FALSE) } # }

title: Extract Text from GAO PDF Reports — extract_text
text: Reads PDF files local directory extracts text content using pdftools::pdf_text(). Designed work PDFs downloaded via auto_download().

title: Extract Text from GAO PDF Reports — extract_text
code: extract_text(pdf_dir, pattern = "\\.pdf$", verbose = TRUE)

title: Extract Text from GAO PDF Reports — extract_text
text: pdf_dir Character. Path directory containing PDF files. pattern Character. Regex pattern filter filenames (default: "\\.pdf$"). verbose Logical. Show progress messages (default: TRUE).

title: Extract Text from GAO PDF Reports — extract_text
text: data.frame columns: file Character. PDF filename (without directory path). text Character. extracted text, pages collapsed single string separated newlines. pages Integer. number pages PDF.

title: Extract Text from GAO PDF Reports — extract_text
text: Requires pdftools package. Install install.packages("pdftools") already available. Files fail parse (e.g., scanned/image-PDFs) included result NA text NA pages along warning.

title: Extract Text from GAO PDF Reports — extract_text
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # After downloading PDFs auto_download(format = "pdf", year = 2024, download_dir = "gao_reports") texts <- extract_text("gao_reports/pdf") head(texts$file) nchar(texts$text[1]) } # }

title: Get GAO Report Data — gao_links
code: gao_links()

title: Get GAO Report Data — gao_links
text: data.frame one row per GAO report three groups columns: Core metadata: url, title, report_id, published, released, summary, page_count (NA PDF available), topics, subject_terms, agencies_affected (semicolon-separated), has_recommendations / n_recommendations, has_matters / n_matters, requester_type ("congressional_request", "statutory_mandate", "cg_initiated", "testimony", "correspondence", "legal_decision"), requester_committees, requester_members (semicolon-separated). Indicator columns (0/1): 31 topic_* columns, 50 agency_* columns frequently reviewed agencies, plus agency_other. Matching exact per semicolon-delimited item; indicators NA source field missing. Derived covariates: issuing_division (GAO unit decoded report ID; NA old numeric IDs), product_type ("report", "testimony", "correspondence", "legal_decision", "legal_other"), pub_month, pub_dow (1 = Monday), pub_fiscal_year fiscal_quarter (federal fiscal year, starts October), election_year, release_lag_days, n_topics, n_subject_terms, requester party covariates requester_party ("R", "D", "", "mixed", NA), requester_majority_status, requester_chamber, requester_bipartisan. Party covariates resolved matching requester names congressional membership data Voteview Congress active publication; populated reports name individual members Congress requesters.

title: gao 0.6.1
text: Fixed daily data updates: new reports now discovered GAO’s official RSS feed change gao.gov broke previous approach. feed ever unavailable, update fails clear error instead quietly adding nothing. Metadata scraping now recognizes gao.gov returns block page instead report page treats failed fetch, rather reading block page content.

title: gao 0.6.0
text: gao_links() now returns additional analysis-ready columns: issuing_division product_type (decoded report IDs), temporal covariates (pub_month, pub_dow, pub_fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, election_year, release_lag_days), scope counts (n_topics, n_subject_terms), congressional requester covariates (requester_party, requester_majority_status, requester_chamber, requester_bipartisan) resolved Voteview membership data. Much cleaner requester fields: stray text longer appears requester_committees / requester_members; multi-word, hyphenated, suffixed member names (Van Hollen, Ros-Lehtinen, Wasserman Schultz) now resolve; House/Senate members share surname longer collide; independents labeled "" majority status resolved via party caucus . Topic agency indicator columns now use exact matching, similar names longer trigger wrong flag; empty source fields yield NA instead zeros. reliable downloads locale-independent date parsing.

title: gao 0.5.0
text: Smaller package: bundled dataset shrank 6.4 MB 3.7 MB. Indicator columns now computed data loaded. New gao_update_data() downloads latest dataset (refreshed daily) without extra software; gao_links() uses automatically. auto_download() offers check updated data interactive sessions.

title: gao 0.4.0
text: New extract_text() extracts text downloaded PDFs (requires pdftools package). dataset gains page_count, topics, subject_terms columns. title, published, released now complete 56,000+ reports, page counts cover 80% . License changed MIT GPL (>= 3).

title: gao 0.3.0
text: Breaking: gao_links() now returns data.frame full report metadata instead character vector URLs. Fiscal-year filtering now uses publication dates rather patterns report IDs, fixing missing years roughly third older reports.

title: gao 0.2.0
text: New auto_download(): load dataset, filter year, download reports one call, interactive prompts confirmation guard accidental mass downloads. Faster PDF downloads (one fewer web request per report).

title: gao 0.1.0
text: Initial release: bundled dataset ~55,000 GAO report URLs (1921–present), gao_links() browsing, batch download reports PDF HTML.
